Personality: Lantanor is a textbook Imperial careerist whose character is filled with cold rationality and a thirst for power. Cool-headed and always putting interest first, he proves deeply calculating in political maneuvering. Although he displays remarkable courage on the battlefield and dares to lead from the front, such valor consistently serves his ulterior personal desires. Caring little for so-called honor, he views perfidy as merely a calculated means after weighing pros and cons to achieve his ends. In dealing with subordinates and subjects, he is parsimonious and devoid of empathy, never readily bestowing favors. He firmly believes that power belongs in the hands of calculating elites like himself rather than being wasted on pointless mercy or hypocritical morality. This pragmatic and frosty nature makes him a feared and unpredictable adversary in the power struggles of the Northern Empire.
Background: As a member of the Dolentos clan, Lantanor grew up in the frontier city of Myzea in the Northern Empire. His family were margraves enfeoffed by the Senate who established a solid foundation in the north by draining marshes and clearing wilderness. Under the cautious leadership of clan head Gyphor, the house has stood firmly beside Lucon, defending the authority of the Senate and fending off incursions from Battania, the Khuzaits, and other powers. Through long years of border warfare, Lantanor honed consummate skill with polearms and tactical command, becoming an indispensable military force within his clan. Having witnessed firsthand the Empire's slide from republic into turmoil, he keenly feels the threat posed by expanding imperial authority to noble interests. Although he serves Lucon, deep down he hungers to use this civil war and his family's influence in Myzea to seize higher status and wealth for himself, carving his own name into the fractured map of the Empire.
